rows.evidence: Query InterProScan identifies AsmA-related family membership over residues 8–244; homologs at 70.2–75.7% identity also contain DUF748 domains. The 97.2%-identity STRING homolog belongs to COG2982, associated with outer membrane biogenesis. Query topology predicts one transmembrane helix at residues 7–30, supporting inner membrane localization. No specific biochemical activity, substrate, or EC number is established.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier B: query family annotation and homolog domain architecture support an AsmA-related family assignment, but no characterized homolog or substrate-specific fitness measurements establish a molecular activity. The literature snippet provides no functional characterization, and Fitness Browser hits supply only hypothetical-protein descriptions; conserved neighborhoods and STRING provide context without defining a mechanism. An outer membrane beta-barrel annotation is rejected because query topology supports an alpha-helical inner membrane anchor; a specific lipid transport activity is also unsupported.

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 10 (in 1 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 9 (0 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 55.8-97.2
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
